revisions.title: Desire replaces the bad as cause
revisions.body: Harmless desire survives even if bad disappears, so bad cannot be friendship's cause. Socrates offers desire as a new candidate, then connects it to need: what lacks something desires it, and the lacking thing is drawn toward its own (oikeion). For Lysis and Menexenus, this makes them akin in some way, but the relation remains open—perhaps soul, character, manner, or form—and is not yet a final definition.
